title: Extract source-verified decoded OBJ dimension resources for EUR and USA
changes: Document the regional resource inventory, explicit unknown catalogs and versioned base dataset contract; select graphics.obj-dimensions as the first migration family without claiming complete ROM extraction.

Add a bounded typed dimension decoder and deterministic source-authenticated manifest, plus rom-data extract/verify commands with verified temporary-directory publication, valid-data reuse and strict corruption/edited-base rejection.
validation: Release targeted tests pass on Linux: 3 core and 6 CLI, including both opt-in exact local regional ROM tests, independent aliases, source roundtrip, distinct manifests, deterministic payloads/reuse/relocation, malformed/bounded files, forged data and four publishers.

Windows GNU compilation is warning-free; the same targeted suites pass under Wine: 3 core and 5 CLI. The first Wine sandbox server-lock failure is retained; the same compiled binaries pass with normal Wine runtime access. The additional symlink rejection test is Unix-only.

Production CLI builds pass without warnings on Linux and Windows GNU; actual Linux and Windows/Wine commands pass help, first extraction, reuse and verification for both regions. Corresponding manifests and decoded files are byte-identical across the two platforms; canonical binaries are restored and verified by SHA-256.
limitations: Only OBJ dimension metadata are decoded. Automatic startup, runtime/guest reads, other asset catalogs, localized data, mods and performance/lifecycle equivalence remain pending; native Windows and crash/power-loss durability are unverified. No canonical binary, export, commit or push was changed.
